title: Derived internal Hom and localization of a bounded localization complex
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$, and use module sheaves and their unbounded derived category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a section $g$, write $\mathcal O[1/g]$ for the sheafification of $V\mapsto\mathcal O(V)[1/g|_V]$, and write $\mathcal O_U$ for the restriction to the slice site $\mathcal C/U$. Let $P^\bullet$ be a bounded complex whose terms are finite direct sums of such localizations (including $\mathcal O=\mathcal O[1/1]$), and let $N\in D(\mathcal O)$. Derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] commutes with slice restriction:
$$R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(P,N)|_U\cong R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(P|_U,N|_U).$$
For any object $U$ and $f\in\mathcal O(U)$ let $P_f^\bullet=\mathcal O_U[1/f]\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}P^\bullet|_U$, with the differential obtained by tensoring. This ordinary complex represents $\mathcal O_U[1/f]\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_U}P|_U$; a summand $\mathcal O_U[1/g]$ becomes $\mathcal O_U[1/(fg)]$. Here the derived tensor is the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] after a K-flat replacement [def-pc-kflat-complex]. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f],R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(P|_U,N|_U))\cong R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(P_f,N|_U),$$
natural in $N$ and chain maps of $P$, and compatible with further slice restriction. These assertions impose no boundedness condition on $N$.

source.place: Tags 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), 08JB (lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U); the localization specialization is also literature/stacks-project/algebraization.tex Tag 0996 (lemma-map-twice-localize), proof and its application in Tag 099B.

proof.text: Choose a representative of $N$ and a K-injective resolution $N^\bullet\to I^\bullet$, using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $H^\bullet=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P^\bullet,I^\bullet)$ represents $R\mathcal Hom(P,N)$. Restriction is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], so $I|_U$ represents $N|_U$, and it is K-injective by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized]. For $V\to U$, the slice defining the sheaf Hom over $V/U$ is $\mathcal C/V$ by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Thus the sheaf Hom formula [def-pur-sheaf-hom] identifies each restricted factor with the corresponding sheaf Hom of restricted modules. Products of sheaves are sectionwise, and the differential $d_I\varphi-(-1)^n\varphi d_P$ is unchanged [def-pur-hom-complex]. Hence $H|_U=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P|_U,I|_U)$ as complexes, giving the first claimed canonical isomorphism.

On the original site or any slice, let $h$ be a global section of its ring sheaf $R$, and let $L_h(V)=R(V)[1/h]$ as a presheaf. For a monomorphism $M'\to M$ of module sheaves, the maps $M'(V)\otimes_{R(V)}L_h(V)\to M(V)\otimes_{R(V)}L_h(V)$ are injective by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. Sheafifying preserves this monomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact]; [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor] identifies it with $M'\otimes_R L_h^\#\to M\otimes_R L_h^\#$. Tensor with $L_h^\#$ preserves cokernels because it is a left adjoint [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. Consequently it is exact, which is precisely flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. A finite direct sum of these sheaves is flat: its tensor functor is the finite direct sum of their exact tensor functors, and kernels and cokernels of finite direct sums are computed componentwise. This argument includes the empty direct sum.

Restriction of a sheafified localization to $\mathcal C/U$ is the sheafification of the restricted presheaf: over $V\to U$ both are obtained by the same local sections, the same covering families and the same equality after a covering; use [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] and the sheafification universal property [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]. Therefore step 2 applies to every term of $P|_U$. Since $P|_U$ is bounded, [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes it K-flat. The same lemma makes $S[0]$ K-flat for $S=\mathcal O_U[1/f]$. In the derived-tensor construction in the statement, take the identity K-flat replacement of $P|_U$. Its total tensor with $S[0]$ has terms $S\otimes P^n|_U$ and differential $1\otimes d_P$ by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], so it is exactly $P_f^\bullet$. Thus the ordinary complex in the statement represents the derived tensor.

For any commutative ring $A$, the bilinear multiplication map gives $A[1/f]\otimes_A A[1/g]\to A[1/(fg)]$. Explicitly, for $k\geq r,s$ it sends $(a/f^r)\otimes(b/g^s)$ to $abf^{k-r}g^{k-s}/(fg)^k$. Its inverse sends $c/(fg)^n$ to $(1/f^n)\otimes(c/g^n)$. The maps respect the fraction equivalence relations and are inverse: inserting the first expression into the second and moving $f^{k-r}$ and $g^{k-s}$ across the tensor sign gives the original pure tensor; the other composite is $c/(fg)^n$. These formulas commute with ring restriction maps. Sheafify this presheaf isomorphism and use [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor] to obtain $\mathcal O_U[1/f]\otimes\mathcal O_U[1/g]\cong\mathcal O_U[1/(fg)]$. Tensor distributes over the finite direct sums since it is a left adjoint [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. This proves the assertion about each summand, without requiring the differential of $P$ to preserve the displayed summands.

source.place: Tag 0996 (lemma-map-twice-localize), proof of (3); fraction calculation made explicit

proof.text: Work now on $\mathcal C/U$ and put $J=I|_U$ and $Q=P|_U$. The complex $J$ is K-injective by step 1 and $Q$ is K-flat by step 3. Hence $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(Q,J)$ is K-injective by [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective]. Applying [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] twice, the left side of the desired currying formula is represented by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(S[0],\mathcal Hom^\bullet(Q,J))$. The right side is represented by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P_f,J)$. The natural chain isomorphism [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total] with $\mathcal K=S[0]$, $\mathcal L=Q$, $\mathcal M=J$ identifies these complexes, since its total tensor argument is $P_f$ by step 3. In degree $n$ the map sends $\varphi$ to the maps $s\otimes q\mapsto\varphi(s)^p(q)$ into $J^{p+n}$; its differential is $d_J\varphi(s)^p(q)-(-1)^n\varphi(s)^{p+1}(d_Qq)$ on both sides because $S$ has degree zero. Localizing this chain isomorphism gives precisely the second claimed canonical isomorphism.

The chain isomorphism in step 5 is natural in the three complexes by [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total]. Choose the functorial K-injective resolutions of [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; their maps and chain maps of $P$ therefore give the required naturality squares. The definition [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] identifies other representatives and resolutions canonically; in particular it sends quasi-isomorphisms in each variable to isomorphisms, so the same naturality holds for morphisms of $N$ in the derived category. For $V\to U$, apply the restriction computation of step 1 to $J$ and to $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(Q,J)$, both K-injective, using [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized]. On a further object $W\to V$, both iterated restrictions evaluate the map in step 5 by exactly $s\otimes q\mapsto\varphi(s)(q)$, and evaluate the fraction maps of step 4 by the same fractions. The relocalization identity [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] makes these equality statements identities over $\mathcal C/W$, so the entire comparison commutes with further slice restriction. No step uses a bound on $J$ or on $N$: boundedness was used only for $P$ in step 3.
